Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 40.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

options.A: Tissues containing collagen fibres cannot stretch.

questions.questionText: Catechol is a chemical found in a number of fruits. Catechol can be oxidised to a quinone by the enzyme catechol oxidase. Catechol oxidase is inhibited by parahydroxybenzoic acid (PHBA), which is structurally similar to catechol. In the presence of PHBA, the Michaelis-Menten constant (K ) for catechol oxidase m increases. How does PHBA inhibit catechol oxidase?
Which statements about the fluid mosaic model of a membrane are correct?

Diagram 1 and diagram 2 show how the transverse section through a leaf changes when the leaf is moved from solution X to solution Y. leaf solution X solution Y diagram 1 diagram 2 Which row describes the water potential of the leaf cells and surrounding solutions in diagram 2 compared with diagram 1? water potential of leaf cells water potential of solution Y in diagram 2 compared with compared with water water potential of leaf cells potential of solution X in diagram 1
Which features must always be present for water to move between two solutions by osmosis?

When living pancreatic cells were placed in a solution of a red stain called neutral red, the cytoplasm became red. The cells were then removed from the solution of neutral red. The red stain in the cytoplasm moved into vesicles, which were exported from the cell, eventually leaving the cell colourless. Which transport mechanisms could explain how the red stain entered and left the cells?

DNA molecules in a eukaryotic cell must be packaged compactly because their combined length is much greater than the diameter of the nucleus. Which structures are required during the process of packaging DNA molecules compactly?
Which statements about mitosis are correct?

A human chromosome is made up of different parts. Some parts of a typical human chromosome are more numerous than others. Which parts are listed in order from least numerous to most numerous in a human white blood cell?
A piece of double-stranded DNA containing 12  103 nucleotides is transcribed and translated to produce a single polypeptide. What is the maximum number of amino acids in this polypeptide?
Which statements about complementary base pairing are correct?
What are the products when a DNA molecule replicates?

options.A: two molecules of DNA each made of a sequence of paired bases
options.B: two molecules of DNA each made of a sequence of paired nucleotides
options.C: two strands of DNA each made of a sequence of paired bases
options.D: two strands of DNA each made of a sequence of paired nucleotides

Some of the parts of a plant root involved in water transport are listed.
What is an example of a mass flow system in a plant?

options.A: the loading of amino acids from the surrounding tissues into companion cells
options.B: the movement of sap through the phloem sieve tubes in the stem
options.C: the movement of water across the root along the symplastic pathway
options.D: the movement of water vapour from the internal spaces in the leaf out through the stomata

questions.questionText: The diameter of a tree trunk usually decreases slightly during the day. Which changes in environmental factors during the day could cause the diameter to decrease even more? increased temperature
Which statement about the role of co-transporter proteins in the movement of sucrose is correct?

options.A: Co-transporter proteins pump hydrogen ions into phloem sieve tubes along with sucrose.
options.B: Hydrogen ions diffuse through co-transporter proteins with sucrose into companion cells.
options.C: Plasmodesmata move sucrose into phloem sieve tubes via co-transporter proteins.
options.D: Sucrose is moved through co-transporter proteins by active transport.

The heart rate of a person at rest was recorded at intervals over two 15-minute periods. During the first five minutes of the second 15-minute period, the person smoked a cigarette. The graph shows the results recorded during the two 15-minute periods. smoking for first five 100 minutes heart rate / beats per min not smoking 0 5 10 15 time / mins What can be concluded from the graph?

options.A: Carbon monoxide affects the heart rate.
options.B: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin increasing the flow of blood.
options.C: Nicotine increases the heart rate so is a stimulant.
options.D: The heart rate increases as a result of smoking.

questions.questionText: Emphysema is a type of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). A person with emphysema has difficulties in breathing out. Why does emphysema cause difficulties in breathing out?

options.A: Smooth muscle fibres in the airways are destroyed.
options.B: Too little mucus is produced in the bronchi.
options.C: The elasticity of the alveoli decreases.
options.D: The surface area of the alveoli becomes larger.
